{
  "items": [
    {
      "category": "support_location_extent",
      "entity": "Location and number of clamped boundary portions Gamma_u",
      "issue": "figure_only",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1.1 identifies the supports only through Fig. 6a. Their locations and number are not described. Coordinates below use the square [0,L] x [0,L].",
      "readings": [
        "A clamped portion of the left edge x=0.",
        "A clamped portion of the bottom edge y=0.",
        "Separate clamped portions on the left and right edges."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "support_location_extent",
      "entity": "Extent of each clamped boundary portion",
      "issue": "figure_only",
      "description": "Neither Sec. 4.1.1 nor the Fig. 6 caption specifies support lengths or endpoints. The zero-displacement condition itself is explicit.",
      "readings": [
        "Clamp the entire selected edge.",
        "Clamp a central patch spanning tangential coordinates 0.4L to 0.6L.",
        "Clamp two end patches spanning 0 to 0.1L and 0.9L to L."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_position",
      "entity": "Number and locations of loaded boundary portions Gamma_t",
      "issue": "figure_only",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1.1 says only 'asymmetrically loaded' and refers to Fig. 6a; no loaded edge, coordinates, or number of patches is given.",
      "readings": [
        "One right-edge patch centered at (L,L/4).",
        "One right-edge patch centered at (L,3L/4).",
        "One top-edge patch centered at (3L/4,L).",
        "Two right-edge patches centered at (L,L/4) and (L,L/2), loaded simultaneously."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_extent_distribution",
      "entity": "Length of the traction application region",
      "issue": "figure_only",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1 specifies a traction magnitude in N/m but does not give the length or endpoints of Gamma_t for Fig. 6a. Consequently, the resultant force is also undetermined.",
      "readings": [
        "Apply the stated traction over a segment of length 0.05L.",
        "Apply it over a segment of length 0.1L.",
        "Apply it over the entire selected edge."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_direction",
      "entity": "Direction of the applied traction",
      "issue": "figure_only",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1 gives only the traction magnitude; Sec. 4.1.1 and the Fig. 6 caption supply no vector components or angle.",
      "readings": [
        "Vertical downward, with unit direction (0,-1).",
        "Horizontal, with unit direction (1,0).",
        "Oblique downward, with unit direction (1,-1)/sqrt(2)."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "passive_region",
      "entity": "Protected material at loads and supports",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Secs. 2.2–3 impose a level-set boundary value on auxiliary G_t, but do not explicitly map that set to physical boundary sets or specify finite passive cell masks for Fig. 6a.",
      "readings": [
        "Map G_t exactly to Gamma_t and impose only boundary values, with no additional passive cells.",
        "Protect one cell of solid material inward from Gamma_t.",
        "Protect one cell inward from both Gamma_t and Gamma_u.",
        "Protect solid pads of depth 0.02L at both loaded and supported portions."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Beta values used in the parameter study",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1.1 states that beta varies between 2 and 8, but does not enumerate the separate runs shown in Fig. 7.",
      "readings": [
        "Run beta values {2,8}.",
        "Run beta values {2,4,6,8}.",
        "Run beta values {2,3,4,5,6,7,8}."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Material indicator used for stiffness and volume",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "Sec. 2.2, Eq. (23), introduces a smooth tanh indicator, whereas Sec. 4.1 explicitly treats Theta as binary when simplifying the Ersatz formulation.",
      "readings": [
        "Use binary Theta=1 for phi>=0 and Theta=0 otherwise in stiffness and volume.",
        "Use Theta=(tanh(2 beta phi)+1)/2 in stiffness and volume."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Ersatz stiffness and sensitivity when using smooth Theta",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "Eq. (40) gives cubic interpolation for q=3, while the subsequent binary identities and Eq. (41) give simplifications that are inequivalent for the smooth indicator of Eq. (23).",
      "readings": [
        "Use cubic stiffness (1-e)Theta^3+e and its exact derivative 3(1-e)Theta^2.",
        "Use cubic stiffness but the simplified Eq. (41) sensitivity 3(1-e)Theta.",
        "Apply the stated binary identities to obtain linear stiffness (1-e)Theta+e, while retaining Eq. (41) for sensitivity."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Level-set Dirichlet value on auxiliary G_t",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "Secs. 2.2–3 and the strong wave problem in Appendix A.1 prescribe phi=1, but the final boundary condition in the Appendix A.1 weak formulation prescribes phi=0.",
      "readings": [
        "Enforce phi=1 on G_t.",
        "Enforce phi=0 on G_t."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "History term in the wave update",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "Eq. (32), the later weak and matrix forms, and Appendix A.1 use the previous field phi_(v-1). Eq. (34) instead subtracts phi_v; with m=k=0 these produce different updates.",
      "readings": [
        "Use right-hand side -S_v+2 phi_v-phi_(v-1).",
        "Follow Eq. (34) literally and use right-hand side -S_v+phi_v."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Numerical values of the initial level-set fields",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1 specifies completely filled initial configurations for phi_0 and phi_(-1), but does not give their numerical amplitudes. Positive fields can describe the same filled topology.",
      "readings": [
        "Set phi_0=phi_(-1)=1 at all free nodes.",
        "Set phi_0=phi_(-1)=0.5 at free nodes, applying prescribed boundary values separately.",
        "Use equal, spatially varying positive initial fields, applying prescribed boundary values separately."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Enforcement of level-set bounds",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 2.1 defines phi within [-1,1], but Sec. 3 does not specify how the linear wave update is kept within those bounds.",
      "readings": [
        "Clip nodal values to [-1,1] after every update and store the clipped history.",
        "Solve each update as a problem with explicit box constraints.",
        "Rescale an overflowing field into [-1,1], then reapply prescribed boundary values."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Sensitivity normalization C_v",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Eq. (44) places an L2(D) magnitude inside another domain integral, leaving unclear whether it denotes a pointwise magnitude or a global norm. Let s(x) denote the equilibrium sensitivity density.",
      "readings": [
        "Use mean absolute sensitivity: C_v=integral_D |s|/(c_f V_0).",
        "Interpret the inner expression as a global L2 norm, giving C_v=sqrt(integral_D s^2)/c_f.",
        "Use root-mean-square sensitivity: C_v=sqrt(integral_D s^2/V_0)/c_f."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Augmented-Lagrangian initialization and penalty schedule",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 4.1 gives multiplier equations and says r increases to r_max, but supplies no initial multiplier, initial penalty, growth rate, or cap. J_init below denotes initial compliance.",
      "readings": [
        "lambda_0=0, r_0=J_init, and r_(n+1)=min(1.05 r_n,1000 J_init).",
        "lambda_0=J_init, r_0=10 J_init, and r_(n+1)=min(1.2 r_n,10000 J_init)."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Timing of multiplier and penalty updates",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Sec. 3 computes sensitivities before the stated multiplier update, while Sec. 4.1 expresses f_1 using lambda and defines an update from lambda-prime without iteration indices. The penalty-update timing is also unspecified.",
      "readings": [
        "Evaluate f_1 with stored lambda and r, then update both for the next iteration.",
        "Update lambda using the current constraint before evaluating f_1; increase r afterward.",
        "Increase r and update lambda before evaluating the current f_1."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Termination criteria and reported final iterate",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 3 mentions convergence or a predefined iteration limit, but gives no tolerances, monitoring window, limit, or rule for selecting an iterate if the undamped update oscillates.",
      "readings": [
        "Stop after 500 updates and report the last iterate.",
        "Stop when relative compliance change and positive volume violation are below 1e-3 for five iterations, with a 1000-iteration cap.",
        "Use thresholds of 1e-4 over ten iterations and a 2000-iteration cap, reporting the best feasible iterate."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "mesh",
      "entity": "Structured-grid resolution corresponding to the adaptive mesh",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 3 uses adaptive mmg refinement; Sec. 4.1 provides only minimum and maximum element sizes. These do not determine element counts, the refinement pattern, or an equivalent fixed structured grid.",
      "readings": [
        "Use a fixed 100 x 100 grid, with cell width 0.01L.",
        "Use a fixed 200 x 200 grid, with cell width 0.005L.",
        "Use a fixed 2000 x 2000 grid, with cell width 0.0005L."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "mesh",
      "entity": "Finite-element spaces for displacement and level set",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 3 introduces unspecified shape functions. Its choice alpha=2 identifies a function-space order and does not specify finite-element polynomial degrees or the relationship between displacement and level-set discretizations.",
      "readings": [
        "Use bilinear quadrilateral elements for both displacement and phi.",
        "Use quadratic quadrilateral elements for both fields.",
        "Use bilinear displacement elements and quadratic level-set elements on the same structured cells."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "mesh",
      "entity": "Integration and conversion of phi into cell properties",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Secs. 3–4.1 give continuum integrals but no quadrature or rule for converting a nodal level set into cell stiffness and material volume, particularly in cells crossed by phi=0.",
      "readings": [
        "Evaluate Theta and tau at quadrature points and integrate their spatial variation.",
        "Evaluate Theta at each cell center and assign constant cell properties.",
        "For a binary indicator, resolve the positive-phi subcell area and integrate solid and Ersatz portions separately."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "mesh",
      "entity": "Transfer of support and traction segments to grid nodes and faces",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "The paper gives no structured-grid rule for segment endpoints that fall between nodes, partial loaded faces, or the corresponding constrained-node selection.",
      "readings": [
        "Choose a grid aligned with all boundary-segment endpoints and assemble consistent boundary loads.",
        "Snap endpoints to the nearest grid nodes and use the resulting whole faces.",
        "Integrate traction over exact partial-face overlaps and constrain nodes lying within each support segment."
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "Numerical solution accuracy for equilibrium and wave systems",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 3 names FreeFEM++ and finite elements but does not state linear solver choices or residual tolerances for either system.",
      "readings": [
        "Use direct factorization for both systems.",
        "Use iterative solves with relative residual tolerance 1e-8.",
        "Use iterative solves with relative residual tolerance 1e-4."
      ],
      "effect": "unsure"
    }
  ]
}

items.entity: Material indicator used for stiffness and volume
items.description: Sec. 2.2, Eq. (23), introduces a smooth tanh indicator, whereas Sec. 4.1 explicitly treats Theta as binary when simplifying the Ersatz formulation.
readings: Use binary Theta=1 for phi>=0 and Theta=0 otherwise in stiffness and volume.
Use Theta=(tanh(2 beta phi)+1)/2 in stiffness and volume.

items.entity: Ersatz stiffness and sensitivity when using smooth Theta
items.description: Eq. (40) gives cubic interpolation for q=3, while the subsequent binary identities and Eq. (41) give simplifications that are inequivalent for the smooth indicator of Eq. (23).
readings: Use cubic stiffness (1-e)Theta^3+e and its exact derivative 3(1-e)Theta^2.
Use cubic stiffness but the simplified Eq. (41) sensitivity 3(1-e)Theta.
Apply the stated binary identities to obtain linear stiffness (1-e)Theta+e, while retaining Eq. (41) for sensitivity.

items.entity: Level-set Dirichlet value on auxiliary G_t
items.description: Secs. 2.2–3 and the strong wave problem in Appendix A.1 prescribe phi=1, but the final boundary condition in the Appendix A.1 weak formulation prescribes phi=0.
readings: Enforce phi=1 on G_t.
Enforce phi=0 on G_t.

items.entity: History term in the wave update
items.description: Eq. (32), the later weak and matrix forms, and Appendix A.1 use the previous field phi_(v-1). Eq. (34) instead subtracts phi_v; with m=k=0 these produce different updates.
readings: Use right-hand side -S_v+2 phi_v-phi_(v-1).
Follow Eq. (34) literally and use right-hand side -S_v+phi_v.

items.entity: Numerical values of the initial level-set fields
items.description: Sec. 4.1 specifies completely filled initial configurations for phi_0 and phi_(-1), but does not give their numerical amplitudes. Positive fields can describe the same filled topology.
readings: Set phi_0=phi_(-1)=1 at all free nodes.
Set phi_0=phi_(-1)=0.5 at free nodes, applying prescribed boundary values separately.
Use equal, spatially varying positive initial fields, applying prescribed boundary values separately.

items.entity: Enforcement of level-set bounds
items.description: Sec. 2.1 defines phi within [-1,1], but Sec. 3 does not specify how the linear wave update is kept within those bounds.
readings: Clip nodal values to [-1,1] after every update and store the clipped history.
Solve each update as a problem with explicit box constraints.
Rescale an overflowing field into [-1,1], then reapply prescribed boundary values.

items.entity: Sensitivity normalization C_v
items.description: Eq. (44) places an L2(D) magnitude inside another domain integral, leaving unclear whether it denotes a pointwise magnitude or a global norm. Let s(x) denote the equilibrium sensitivity density.
readings: Use mean absolute sensitivity: C_v=integral_D |s|/(c_f V_0).
Interpret the inner expression as a global L2 norm, giving C_v=sqrt(integral_D s^2)/c_f.
Use root-mean-square sensitivity: C_v=sqrt(integral_D s^2/V_0)/c_f.

items.entity: Augmented-Lagrangian initialization and penalty schedule
items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives multiplier equations and says r increases to r_max, but supplies no initial multiplier, initial penalty, growth rate, or cap. J_init below denotes initial compliance.
readings: lambda_0=0, r_0=J_init, and r_(n+1)=min(1.05 r_n,1000 J_init).
lambda_0=J_init, r_0=10 J_init, and r_(n+1)=min(1.2 r_n,10000 J_init).

items.entity: Timing of multiplier and penalty updates
items.description: Sec. 3 computes sensitivities before the stated multiplier update, while Sec. 4.1 expresses f_1 using lambda and defines an update from lambda-prime without iteration indices. The penalty-update timing is also unspecified.
readings: Evaluate f_1 with stored lambda and r, then update both for the next iteration.
Update lambda using the current constraint before evaluating f_1; increase r afterward.
Increase r and update lambda before evaluating the current f_1.

items.entity: Termination criteria and reported final iterate
items.description: Sec. 3 mentions convergence or a predefined iteration limit, but gives no tolerances, monitoring window, limit, or rule for selecting an iterate if the undamped update oscillates.
readings: Stop after 500 updates and report the last iterate.
Stop when relative compliance change and positive volume violation are below 1e-3 for five iterations, with a 1000-iteration cap.
Use thresholds of 1e-4 over ten iterations and a 2000-iteration cap, reporting the best feasible iterate.

items.entity: Structured-grid resolution corresponding to the adaptive mesh
items.description: Sec. 3 uses adaptive mmg refinement; Sec. 4.1 provides only minimum and maximum element sizes. These do not determine element counts, the refinement pattern, or an equivalent fixed structured grid.
readings: Use a fixed 100 x 100 grid, with cell width 0.01L.
Use a fixed 200 x 200 grid, with cell width 0.005L.
Use a fixed 2000 x 2000 grid, with cell width 0.0005L.

items.entity: Finite-element spaces for displacement and level set
items.description: Sec. 3 introduces unspecified shape functions. Its choice alpha=2 identifies a function-space order and does not specify finite-element polynomial degrees or the relationship between displacement and level-set discretizations.
readings: Use bilinear quadrilateral elements for both displacement and phi.
Use quadratic quadrilateral elements for both fields.
Use bilinear displacement elements and quadratic level-set elements on the same structured cells.

items.entity: Integration and conversion of phi into cell properties
items.description: Secs. 3–4.1 give continuum integrals but no quadrature or rule for converting a nodal level set into cell stiffness and material volume, particularly in cells crossed by phi=0.
readings: Evaluate Theta and tau at quadrature points and integrate their spatial variation.
Evaluate Theta at each cell center and assign constant cell properties.
For a binary indicator, resolve the positive-phi subcell area and integrate solid and Ersatz portions separately.

items.entity: Transfer of support and traction segments to grid nodes and faces
items.description: The paper gives no structured-grid rule for segment endpoints that fall between nodes, partial loaded faces, or the corresponding constrained-node selection.
readings: Choose a grid aligned with all boundary-segment endpoints and assemble consistent boundary loads.
Snap endpoints to the nearest grid nodes and use the resulting whole faces.
Integrate traction over exact partial-face overlaps and constrain nodes lying within each support segment.

items.entity: Numerical solution accuracy for equilibrium and wave systems
items.description: Sec. 3 names FreeFEM++ and finite elements but does not state linear solver choices or residual tolerances for either system.
readings: Use direct factorization for both systems.
Use iterative solves with relative residual tolerance 1e-8.
Use iterative solves with relative residual tolerance 1e-4.
